Reduce Motion listing copy vs animation engineering — two different jobs

US/EU indie teams conflate in-app motion reduction with storefront language. Connect and Xcode actually separate them:

  • Reduce Motion in the app — UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled checks, UIViewPropertyAnimator fallbacks, SwiftUI withAnimation guards, parallax removal, and cross-fade transitions instead of zoom effects. Engineering inside the binary — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Animation and motion implementation — Core Animation tuning, Lottie playback policies, and scroll-behavior adjustments when system Reduce Motion is on. Engineering — not listing rewrite.
  • Motion-accessibility marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app respects Reduce Motion or offers fewer animations. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Reduce Motion support in the app.

A Reduce Motion-compatible app and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe less animation on the store page, not whether animations actually tone down inside the app.

Reduce Motion-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Motion-accessibility marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe animation reduction — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Reduce Motion vs generic "less animation"

US pages use "Respects Reduce Motion", "Reduced motion", or "Fewer animations." China storefront copy often uses 尊重系统减少动态效果设置, 减少动态效果, 动画更克制, or 降低动画强度 — depending on whether you mean Apple's Reduce Motion setting specifically, optional in-app animation toggles, or general motion-sensitive design. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual motion scope, not inventing Reduce Motion support your app does not ship.

Reduce Motion vs VoiceOver — do not conflate

Respecting system Reduce Motion is motion-accessibility marketing — screen reader support is VoiceOver copy. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 旁白支持 when your English source only markets less animation. If you ship both, say both accurately; if you ship motion reduction only, keep VoiceOver vocabulary out of subtitle, keywords, and overlays.

No medical or vestibular-disorder claims

US marketing sometimes mentions motion sickness, vestibular sensitivity, or dizziness relief. zh-Hans listing copy should describe animation behavior and system-setting respect — not medical treatment, diagnosis, or therapeutic outcomes. AppLocale rewrites motion-accessibility storefront language; we do not write health claims or sell audit retainers.

Listing text vs re-shooting animation demos

You can describe Reduce Motion accurately in zh-Hans description, subtitle, and overlay lines without re-exporting every gallery frame as a before/after animation comparison. If your English gallery already shows motion on/off pairs, send those overlay strings and we localize them. AppLocale does not shoot, design, or re-export screenshots.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need motion-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 减少动态效果, 降低动画, and 少动画 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Respects Reduce Motion" headlines on gallery frames showing Settings → Accessibility → Motion — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

Promotional text refreshes

Motion-accessibility launches and animation-reduction milestone updates often land in the 170-character promotional text field above the description — updatable without a new binary. Why English-only Reduce Motion copy hurts China storefront conversion

Motion-sensitive purchasers browsing the China App Store evaluate animation claims in the first scroll. Common failure modes when only en-US is filled:

  • Localized listing, English badges — description promises Chinese motion support; screenshot overlays still "Fewer animations" at the worst moment
  • Search intent miss — buyers search 减少动态效果 or 降低动画; English-only keywords miss intent even when Reduce Motion works in the app
  • Competitor contrast — rivals with native zh-Hans motion-accessibility copy look more serious about China buyers who prefer less animation
  • Overclaim risk in translation — machine-translated strings that upgrade "toned-down transitions" to full medical relief claims, or imply VoiceOver when only animation was reduced

Clearer zh-Hans motion marketing reduces confusion on the product page. It does not replace animation checks in the binary, third-party accessibility audits, or in-app motion settings.

Why machine-translated Reduce Motion copy fails

  • Literal "Reduce Motion" → awkward 减少运动 instead of commerce-idiomatic 减少动态效果 (matches iOS Settings → 辅助功能 → 动态效果 vocabulary)
  • Generic "less animation" → 更少的动画 instead of buyer-friendly 动画更克制 or 降低动画强度
  • English badge headlines preserved on zh-Hans screenshots — "Respects Reduce Motion" with no Chinese benefit line beside it
  • Overlay text overflow — long English motion captions pasted into short screenshot callout zones truncate on device

  • Medical phrasing drift — 晕动症治疗 or vestibular-disorder treatment language when English only described respecting system settings

Machine translation is fine for internal drafts. Motion-accessibility copy appears on screenshot galleries and in description skims. Strong Chinese strings lead with the benefit and state scope plainly:

zh-Hans and en-US strings can differ in length and structure when the underlying motion story is the same — avoid mirroring English comma-heavy promo lines character-for-character.
